CyberCloud.Cache/redis.title: Valkey cache
CyberCloud.Cache/redis.summary: A managed Valkey cache with Sentinel failover, on spotahome/redis-operator. Valkey rather than Redis, per ADR-011; every Redis client works against it.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the cache is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Valkey cache to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The cache's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster whose namespace holds the RedisFailover.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Valkey cache to change it.

fields.name: maxmemoryPolicy
fields.label: Maxmemory policy
fields.hint: What happens when the cache reaches its memory limit. noeviction returns an error to the writer rather than dropping a key somebody is relying on.

fields.name: mode
fields.label: Mode
fields.hint: Replication topology. Sentinel is the only one this operator implements, and a client written against it is not portable to a sharded deployment, so it may not change after create.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Valkey cache to change it.

fields.name: monitoring
fields.label: Monitoring
fields.hint: What the platform scrapes.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether the operator runs a metrics exporter beside every Valkey and every Sentinel pod.

fields.name: persistence
fields.label: Persistence
fields.hint: What survives a restart. None of the three settings makes a cache a database.

fields.name: class
fields.label: Class
fields.hint: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Valkey cache to change it.

fields.name: fsync
fields.label: Fsync
fields.hint: How often the append-only file reaches the disk. Read only when the mode is AOF; everysec can lose the last second of writes.

fields.name: mode
fields.label: Mode
fields.hint: None keeps nothing, RDB snapshots periodically, AOF appends every write.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: Persistent volume size in Kubernetes quantity form. Unused when the mode is None, which keeps the data directory in memory.

fields.name: replicas
fields.label: Replicas
fields.hint: Number of Valkey instances, including the primary. One is a single point of failure and is offered for development only.

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory, either by preset or explicitly.

fields.name: cpu
fields.label: Cpu
fields.hint: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: memory
fields.label: Memory
fields.hint: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset. It also sets maxmemory, so a cache evicts or refuses before the kernel kills the pod.

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Caches use the m1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 8 GiB.

fields.name: version
fields.label: Version
fields.hint: Major Valkey version. Minor upgrades are applied automatically in the maintenance window.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.DBforPostgreSQL/servers.summary: A managed PostgreSQL cluster on CloudNativePG, with replication, PgBouncer and backup to the tenant's object store.

fields.name: location

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties

fields.name: backup
fields.label: Backup
fields.hint: Backup to the tenant's object store, using CloudNativePG's barman-cloud.

fields.name: destinationPath

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether continuous backup and WAL archiving run.

fields.name: retentionDays
fields.label: Retention days
fields.hint: How long base backups and WAL are kept. The point-in-time-recovery window is this number of days.

fields.name: bootstrap
fields.label: Bootstrap

fields.name: database

fields.hint: Name of the application database created on first start.

fields.name: owner
fields.label: Owner

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster whose namespace holds the CloudNativePG objects.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new PostgreSQL server to change it.

fields.name: extensions
fields.label: Extensions
fields.hint: Extensions to install, from the platform allow-list. An arbitrary-extension escape hatch is a code-execution surface and is not offered.

fields.name: monitoring
fields.label: Monitoring
fields.hint: What the platform scrapes.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether CloudNativePG emits a PodMonitor for the platform's metrics stack.

fields.name: pooling
fields.label: Pooling
fields.hint: PgBouncer in front of the cluster.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether to run a connection pooler. On by default — a managed Postgres without one fails at the first serverless workload, and adding it later changes the connection string.

fields.name: instances
fields.label: Instances
fields.hint: Number of pooler pods.

fields.name: mode
fields.label: Mode
fields.hint: PgBouncer pooling mode. Transaction pooling is the useful one and breaks session-scoped features such as prepared statements and advisory locks.

fields.name: replicas
fields.label: Replicas
fields.hint: Number of instances, including the primary. One is a single point of failure and is offered for development only.

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory, either by preset or explicitly.

fields.name: cpu
fields.label: Cpu
fields.hint: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: memory
fields.label: Memory
fields.hint: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Databases use the s1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 4 GiB.

fields.name: storage
fields.label: Storage
fields.hint: The data volume.

fields.name: class
fields.label: Class
fields.hint: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new PostgreSQL server to change it.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: Data volume size in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

fields.name: walSize
fields.label: Wal size
fields.hint: Size of the separate write-ahead-log volume. Empty means the WAL shares the data volume.

fields.name: synchronousReplication
fields.label: Synchronous replication
fields.hint: Whether commits wait for a replica. Costs write latency and removes the window in which a failover loses transactions.

fields.name: version
fields.label: Version
fields.hint: Major PostgreSQL version. Minor upgrades are applied automatically in the maintenance window.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Messaging/kafkaClusters.title: Kafka cluster
CyberCloud.Messaging/kafkaClusters.summary: A managed Apache Kafka cluster on Strimzi in KRaft mode, with Cruise Control, configurable retention and an optional firewalled external listener.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the cluster is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Kafka cluster to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The cluster's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster whose namespace holds the Strimzi objects.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Kafka cluster to change it.

fields.name: cruiseControl
fields.label: Cruise control
fields.hint: Cruise Control — partition rebalancing and broker-load reporting.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether Cruise Control runs. On by default: docs/plan/12 puts it in the chart rather than in a follow-up, because rebalancing a Kafka cluster by hand is the operational cost that makes this the most demanding service in the catalogue.

fields.name: external
fields.label: External
fields.hint: Exposure outside the cluster, via a load balancer and a firewall allow-list.

fields.name: allowedCidrs
fields.label: Allowed cidrs
fields.hint: Source ranges permitted to reach the external listener. Required in substance rather than in schema: an empty list with external exposure on renders a load balancer that accepts nothing, which is the safe reading of an unfinished configuration.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether the cluster is reachable from outside the Kubernetes cluster. Off by default — docs/plan/12 § Cross-cutting decisions makes external exposure never the default, because a managed broker on a public IP with a weak password is the most common cloud breach there is.

fields.name: listener
fields.label: Listener
fields.hint: The in-cluster listener every client reaches.

fields.name: tls
fields.label: Tls
fields.hint: Whether the in-cluster listener requires TLS. On by default; turning it off is a plaintext broker on the pod network.

fields.name: monitoring
fields.label: Monitoring
fields.hint: What the platform scrapes.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether the operator runs a Kafka Exporter alongside the cluster, exposing consumer-lag and topic metrics to the platform's metrics stack.

fields.name: nodes
fields.label: Nodes
fields.hint: Number of Kafka nodes, each acting as both a KRaft controller and a broker. Use an odd number: a quorum of two tolerates no failures, and one is a single point of failure offered for development only.

fields.name: retention
fields.label: Retention
fields.hint: How long the cluster keeps messages by default. docs/plan/12 calls retention sizing an ongoing operational concern rather than a one-time setting.

fields.name: hours
fields.label: Hours
fields.hint: Default retention in hours. A week by default.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: Default retention by partition size, in Kubernetes quantity form. Empty means retention is by time alone.

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory per node, either by preset or explicitly.

fields.name: cpu
fields.label: Cpu
fields.hint: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: memory
fields.label: Memory
fields.hint: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Brokers use the c1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 2 GiB and guaranteed rather than burstable.

fields.name: storage
fields.label: Storage
fields.hint: The log volume, per node.

fields.name: class
fields.label: Class
fields.hint: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Kafka cluster to change it.

fields.name: deleteClaim
fields.label: Delete claim
fields.hint: Whether deleting the resource also deletes the log volumes. Off by default, so a mistaken delete leaves the data recoverable by hand.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: Log volume size per node, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

fields.name: topics
fields.label: Topics
fields.hint: Defaults applied to topics the cluster creates automatically. A topic created explicitly overrides them.

fields.name: minInSyncReplicas
fields.label: Min in sync replicas
fields.hint: How many replicas must acknowledge a write before it is committed. Must be below the replication factor, or the cluster cannot tolerate one broker restart.

fields.name: partitions
fields.label: Partitions
fields.hint: Default partition count for a new topic.

fields.name: replicationFactor
fields.label: Replication factor
fields.hint: Default replication factor for a new topic. Must not exceed the node count, or every produce to a new topic fails.

fields.name: version
fields.label: Version
fields.hint: Apache Kafka version. Minor upgrades are applied automatically in the maintenance window; a major upgrade is an explicit update to this field.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Messaging/natsClusters.title: NATS cluster
CyberCloud.Messaging/natsClusters.summary: A managed NATS cluster with JetStream on file storage, optional leaf-node connectivity and an optional firewalled external listener.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the cluster is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new NATS cluster to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The cluster's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster whose namespace holds the NATS servers.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new NATS cluster to change it.

fields.name: external
fields.label: External
fields.hint: Exposure outside the cluster, via a load balancer and a firewall allow-list.

fields.name: allowedCidrs
fields.label: Allowed cidrs
fields.hint: Source ranges permitted to reach the external listener. Required in substance rather than in schema: an empty list with external exposure on renders a load balancer that accepts nothing, which is the safe reading of an unfinished configuration.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether the cluster is reachable from outside the Kubernetes cluster. Off by default — docs/plan/12 § Cross-cutting decisions makes external exposure never the default, because a managed broker on a public IP with a weak password is the most common cloud breach there is.

fields.name: jetstream
fields.label: Jetstream
fields.hint: JetStream — the persistence layer streams and consumers live in. docs/plan/12 has it on unconditionally, so there is no switch to turn it off.

fields.name: maxMemoryStore
fields.label: Max memory store
fields.hint: Ceiling for memory-backed streams, in Kubernetes quantity form. Empty means no memory store at all, so every stream is file-backed — which is what docs/plan/12 asks for and what the volume above is sized for. A value here must leave room for the server itself inside the container's memory limit.

fields.name: leafNodes
fields.label: Leaf nodes
fields.hint: Leaf-node connectivity — docs/plan/12: "so a tenant's edge can attach".

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether the servers accept leaf-node connections. Off by default: a leaf node joins the cluster's subject space, so it is a topology change rather than a client.

fields.name: limits
fields.label: Limits
fields.hint: Server limits a client can run into.

fields.name: maxConnections
fields.label: Max connections
fields.hint: Largest number of client connections one server accepts.

fields.name: maxPayload
fields.label: Max payload
fields.hint: Largest message a client may publish, in bytes. Raising it costs memory on every server, because a server buffers a whole message before routing it.

fields.name: monitoring
fields.label: Monitoring
fields.hint: What the platform scrapes.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether a PodMonitor selects these servers' monitoring endpoint. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". The endpoint itself is always served; this decides whether anything scrapes it.

fields.name: servers
fields.label: Servers
fields.hint: Number of NATS servers. docs/plan/12 says three or five: JetStream replicates through a Raft group, so an even count buys no extra fault tolerance over the odd count below it. One is offered for development only and has no quorum at all.

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory per server, either by preset or explicitly.

fields.name: cpu
fields.label: Cpu
fields.hint: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: memory
fields.label: Memory
fields.hint: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Brokers use the c1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 2 GiB and guaranteed rather than burstable.

fields.name: storage
fields.label: Storage
fields.hint: The JetStream file store, per server.

fields.name: class
fields.label: Class
fields.hint: StorageClass name. Empty means the cluster default.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new NATS cluster to change it.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: JetStream file-store volume size per server, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

fields.name: version
fields.label: Version
fields.hint: NATS server version. Minor upgrades are applied automatically in the maintenance window; a major upgrade is an explicit update to this field.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Search/services.title: OpenSearch service
CyberCloud.Search/services.summary: A managed OpenSearch cluster on the OpenSearch operator, with dedicated cluster-manager, data and optional coordinating node pools and operator-generated transport and HTTP TLS.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the service is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new OpenSearch service to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The service's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster whose namespace holds the search service.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new OpenSearch service to change it.

fields.name: coordinatingNodes
fields.label: Coordinating nodes
fields.hint: Number of coordinating-only nodes — nodes that hold no data and no cluster state and exist to fan a search out and merge the results. Zero is the default and is right until a query pattern makes one data node the bottleneck for every search. They are sized by the same preset as the data nodes.

fields.name: dataNodes
fields.label: Data nodes
fields.hint: Number of data nodes. This is the capacity axis: total raw capacity is this count times the disk size below, before replicas. Every data node also carries the ingest role, so an indexing pipeline needs no separate pool.

fields.name: masterNodes
fields.label: Master nodes
fields.hint: Number of dedicated cluster-manager nodes. They hold the cluster state in a quorum, so three is the smallest count that survives losing one. One is offered for development and has no quorum at all. An even count is worse than the odd count below it and the API cannot say so — see the service's own documentation.

fields.name: monitoring
fields.label: Monitoring
fields.hint: What the platform scrapes.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether the operator is asked for a ServiceMonitor. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". ⚠ The metrics themselves come from the prometheus-exporter plugin, which the operator installs into every node on the first reconcile after this is turned on — so turning it on restarts the pods and turning it off does not remove the plugin.

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory per data node and per coordinating node, either by preset or explicitly. The cluster-manager nodes are sized by the platform and are not affected.

fields.name: cpu
fields.label: Cpu
fields.hint: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: memory
fields.label: Memory
fields.hint: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 8Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Search nodes use the m1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 8 GiB, because OpenSearch is bound by heap and by the filesystem cache rather than by CPU. The m1 rungs below m1.small are deliberately not offered: OpenSearch derives its JVM heap from the container limit and a node under 4 GiB fails a bootstrap check after passing its readiness probe.

fields.name: storage
fields.label: Storage
fields.hint: The data volume, per data node.

fields.name: class
fields.label: Class
fields.hint: StorageClass name for every node pool. Empty means the cluster default.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new OpenSearch service to change it.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: Disk size per data node, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks. The cluster-manager and coordinating nodes get a fixed 10Gi that is not configurable and is counted against the storage quota anyway.

fields.name: version
fields.label: Version
fields.hint: OpenSearch version. ⚠ OpenSearch is a fork of Elasticsearch 7.10 (ADR-011 — Elasticsearch is SSPL and is not available to us) and the two have diverged since, so an Elasticsearch 8 client is not promised anything here. Upgrades between the values below are online and in the maintenance window; a third value is a new api-version.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

CyberCloud.Storage/accounts.title: Storage account
CyberCloud.Storage/accounts.summary: A managed S3-compatible object store on SeaweedFS, with replicated volume servers, a filer and a scalable S3 gateway.

fields.name: location
fields.label: Location
fields.hint: The region the account is billed in.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Storage account to change it.

fields.name: properties
fields.label: Properties
fields.hint: The account's own settings.

fields.name: clusterId
fields.label: Cluster id
fields.hint: The cluster whose namespace holds the object store.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Storage account to change it.

fields.name: gateway
fields.label: Gateway
fields.hint: The S3 gateway — docs/plan/15's ADR-008: "the API is S3".

fields.name: replicas
fields.label: Replicas
fields.hint: Number of S3 gateway pods. The gateway is stateless, so this is a throughput and availability setting rather than a topology one.

fields.name: masters
fields.label: Masters
fields.hint: Number of master servers. The masters hold the volume topology in a Raft group, so three is the smallest count that survives losing one. One is offered for development and has no quorum at all.

fields.name: monitoring
fields.label: Monitoring
fields.hint: What the platform scrapes.

fields.name: enabled
fields.label: Enabled
fields.hint: Whether the operator is asked for a ServiceMonitor per component. On by default — docs/plan/12: "a managed service the tenant cannot see the health of is a black box they will not trust with production". Turning it off removes the metrics port as well as the scrape, which is the operator's own behaviour rather than this provider's.

fields.name: replication
fields.label: Replication
fields.hint: Where the second copy of every object is placed. None keeps one copy and is for scratch data only. A placement the cluster's topology cannot satisfy leaves volumes read-only rather than failing the create. Immutable, because SeaweedFS applies this to volumes as they are created and never rewrites the ones that already exist — a change would split the account into two durability promises with no way to tell which object got which.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Storage account to change it.

fields.name: sizing
fields.label: Sizing
fields.hint: CPU and memory per volume server, either by preset or explicitly. The masters, the filer and the S3 gateway are sized by the platform and are not affected.

fields.name: cpu
fields.label: Cpu
fields.hint: Explicit vCPU quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 500m or 2. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: memory
fields.label: Memory
fields.hint: Explicit memory quantity in Kubernetes form, for example 4Gi. Empty means take it from the preset.

fields.name: preset
fields.label: Preset
fields.hint: A sizing preset from docs/plan/12. Volume servers use the s1 family, which is 1 vCPU to 4 GiB.

fields.name: storage
fields.label: Storage
fields.hint: The data volume, per volume server.

fields.name: class
fields.label: Class
fields.hint: StorageClass name for the volume servers. Empty means the cluster default.
fields.disabledReason: This value cannot change after the resource is created. Create a new Storage account to change it.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: Data volume size per volume server, in Kubernetes quantity form. Grows online; never shrinks.

fields.name: version
fields.label: Version
fields.hint: SeaweedFS version. ⚠ SeaweedFS ships a release roughly weekly and maintains no long-term branch, so docs/plan/12's "supported major versions" is a shape this project does not have; the two values here are the two most recent releases and a new api-version is what adds a third.

fields.name: volumeServers
fields.label: Volume servers
fields.hint: Number of volume servers. This is the capacity axis: total raw capacity is this count times the volume size below, before replication.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.

fields.name: size
fields.label: Size
fields.hint: The bucket's size limit, in Kubernetes quantity form. Empty means no limit other than the account's own provisioned capacity. ⚠ This is a limit inside capacity the account already reserved; it does not add any, and it is not what the bucket is billed on.

fields.name: versioning
fields.label: Versioning
fields.hint: Whether the bucket keeps previous versions of an overwritten object. Off by default. ⚠ docs/plan/15 § Object storage: SeaweedFS' S3 implementation is "good but not complete" and names object versioning as one of the partial areas, so the supported-operations table for the deployed version — not this property — is what says how completely it behaves.

fields.name: tags
fields.label: Tags
fields.hint: Key/value tags, at most 50 pairs — docs/plan/06 § Tags, locks. Values are strings; the cap applies to the merged set, so a PATCH that adds one tag to a full bag is refused.
